citation: Qian, Zhou, Wang, Peng, Yi, Zhao, Huang, Xie & Nie (2025), arXiv 2502.08127v3 (Fino1 / Fin-o1; FinReason). Read: abstract page and v3 HTML
text_source: FinReason eval: FinQA 1,100, DocMath SimpLong 100, CompLong 300 (about 40K tokens), XBRL-Math 90; FinCoT training 9,186 GPT-4o CoT pairs from seven QA sets. Licences MIT and CDLA-Permissive 2.0 for eval sets
feature: Numeric financial QA over tables, long multi-table documents and XBRL equations; auto-gradable (numeric answer extracted, LLM judge compares, judge unnamed)
method: Fin-o1-8B/14B on Qwen3: SFT on filtered CoT then GRPO; PPO and DPO compared; 29 models zero-shot
outcome: Fin-o1-14B avg 61.07, 8B 59.95 vs GPT-4o 61.01, DeepSeek-R1 60.87, Qwen3-8B 52.28; CompLong 26-27 vs 39-42 for frontier; QwQ-32B 52.92 < Qwen2.5-32B 56.17; GRPO +1.4 over SFT
incremental_to: Backbones; general reasoning models (o1, R1, QwQ); Fin-R1, DianJin-R1
pit_handling: Not addressed; FinQA and DocMath feed both training and evaluation, overlap unchecked
informs_decision: Small-vs-large: CoT SFT closes most of the gap in distribution, not on long multi-table; general reasoning tuning does not transfer to finance. 'Reasoning' benchmark is numeric only (S1 B2 territory)

citation: Liu, Guo, Yang, Lou, Zeng and 12 others (2025), arXiv 2503.16252v3 (Fin-R1). Read: abstract page and v3 HTML incl. appendix
text_source: Fin-R1-Data 60,091 Chinese/English items (FinQA, ConvFinQA, Finance-Instruct-500K, FinanceIQ, Ant-Finance, closed postgraduate exam set); DeepSeek-R1 traces filtered by Qwen2.5-72B
feature: Eval: FinQA, ConvFinQA (numeric), Ant_Finance (knowledge MCQ), TFNS (sentiment), Finance-Instruct-500K; LLM-judge graded on 100-point scale
method: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, SFT on distilled traces then GRPO (binary format reward, accuracy judged by Qwen2.5-Max)
outcome: Fin-R1 avg 75.2 vs DeepSeek-R1 78.2, Qwen2.5-7B 65.6; tops FinQA 76 and ConvFinQA 85; below base on Ant (81 vs 85); R1-Distill-Qwen-7B 58.0 < Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 65.6; GRPO-only 67.8, SFT-only 71.9
pit_handling: Not addressed; FinQA/ConvFinQA in training sources and evaluation
informs_decision: Small-vs-large: in-distribution parity claim; independent tests (FinIndices, DocMath) show no transfer. General R1 distillation hurts finance at 7B-14B. SFT does most of the work, RL a few points

citation: Shetty, Upadhayaya, Shah, Nayak, Fee & Jagabathula (2025), FinLLM@IJCAI 2025, arXiv 2507.02954v2. Read: v2 HTML
text_source: Mock CFA Level III (commercial prep provider): 60 MCQ in 10 vignettes; 43 essay questions in 11 vignettes, 149 points
feature: Portfolio-management vignettes: MCQ (auto-gradable, exact match) and essays (rubric, LLM judge GPT-4.1 plus one certified human grader)
method: 23 models; zero-shot, CoT self-consistency N=3/5, Self-Discover; LLM-graded essays; human-graded essays for CoT N=3
outcome: o4-mini composite 79.1; MCQ tops cluster 71-75%; human-graded essays: top closed 79.9-83.2, Llama 3.3 70B 57.7, Llama 3.1 8B 38.9; reasoning vs non-reasoning essays 73.7 vs 61.8; human-LLM identical score ~70% of questions, human +5.6 points
incremental_to: Prompting strategies; closed vs open; reasoning vs non-reasoning
informs_decision: Written synthesis separates models where MCQ does not; 8B scores about half a frontier model. Rubric grading needs human-agreement check (30% disagreement)

citation: Tong, Zhang, Tang, Yang, Hu, Lin, Shi, Zeng, Yang, Zhao, Wei, Qu & Liu (2026), arXiv 2607.28661v1 (FinIndices). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML (Appendices C-D by title)
text_source: Real statements (BS, IS, CF; consolidated and parent) of 829 listed firms (Chinese standards), 384 indices, 28 periods; 640 expert-audited test items, mean 16K tokens; Hugging Face
feature: Single-Index and Table-Index computation needing temporal de-cumulation (YTD to quarter, TTM), stock-flow caliber matching, domain definitions; distractor periods; 'Insufficient information' traps; hint vs no-hint arm; auto-graded numeric equivalence, tables all-or-nothing
method: Automated synthesis pipeline plus three expert auditors (majority vote); 16 models; SFT of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on 6,301 Gemini trajectories
outcome: Gemini-3.1-Pro 79.61/70.70 with hint vs 64.90/38.22 without; Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 62.40/26.50 with hint; Fin-o1-14B 28.16/2.67; Fin-R1 10.87/0.00; SFT +8.54 single, +3.82 table (no hint)
incremental_to: Hint vs no-hint; frontier vs finance-tuned models
pit_handling: Not addressed; labels computed from statements so outcome recall irrelevant; formula recall controlled by hint arm
informs_decision: Template for an S1 reasoning tier: rule labels, auto-graded, far from ceiling once formula withheld and periods combined. Finance-tuned small models collapse: their FinQA gains do not transfer

citation: Zhang, Cao & Liao (2025), Findings of ACL 2025, pp. 8715-8758 (XFinBench). Read: ACL Anthology page and arXiv 2508.15861v1 HTML (first two-thirds)
text_source: 4,235 items from three graduate finance textbooks, rewritten to closed form by GPT-4o (35.2% discarded); 1,000 val / 3,235 test; test answers withheld
feature: Five capabilities: terminology, temporal reasoning, future forecasting, scenario planning, numerical modelling; formats true/false, 3-option MCQ, numeric (within 0.5%); all auto-gradable
method: 18 models, CoT and PoT; retrieval and oracle knowledge arms; three master's-level experts on 1,000 items
outcome: o1 67.3 overall, GPT-4o 63.6, Llama-3.1-8B 45.5, experts 79.8; temporal: o1-preview 59.1, GPT-4o 41.4, Llama-3.1-8B 11.7, experts 79.5; scenario: 60.1 / 46.3 / 22.3 / 75.8
pit_handling: Test answers withheld; textbook memorisation not tested
informs_decision: Auto-gradable formats for temporal reasoning and scenario planning; these are where an 8B trails most. Needs chance correction for true/false and MCQ

citation: Li, Yue, Xu and others (2025), Findings of ACL 2025, pp. 25366-25394; arXiv 2502.12143v3. Read: abstract page and v3 HTML
text_source: Comparable domain (math): MATH train 7,500 prompts; eval MATH, GSM8K, AMC 2023, AIME 2024, OlympiadBench
feature: Learnability of long vs short CoT and large vs small teacher traces by students of 0.5B to 70B
method: Full fine-tuning (<14B) on rejection-sampled teacher traces; Mix Distillation (1:4 long:short)
outcome: Qwen 0.5B/1.5B/3B: short CoT beats long (19.5 vs 14.8; 34.2 vs 27.0; 43.4 vs 40.3); long wins from 7B; small teacher better for <=1.5B; Mix at 3B 45.9 vs 43.4
informs_decision: S1 distillation: for a 0.8B student a 4B teacher and short traces are the better default; test short vs long vs mix if reasoning items are added

citation: Ben Yoash, Brief, Ovadia, Shenderovitz, Mishaeli, Lemberg & Sheetrit (2025), GEM2 workshop at ACL 2025; arXiv 2504.04596v1 (SECQUE). Read: abstract page and v1 HTML
text_source: 45 10-K/10-Q filings of 29 US companies, 2018-2024; 565 expert questions with free-text gold and gold page chunks; Hugging Face
feature: Analyst-style QA: comparison and trend 220, ratio 188, risk factors 85, analyst insights 72; free text graded by SECQUE-Judge (GPT-4o x5, 0/1/2, thresholds tuned on human labels)
method: Gold context in prompt; table renderings, prompt and CoT variants; judge validated on 62 questions / 124 answers
outcome: Strict: GPT-4o 0.69, Llama-3.3-70B 0.65, Qwen2.5-32B 0.61, Phi-4 0.56, Llama-3.1-8B 0.48; judge F1(correct) 0.85, 3-class accuracy 0.75; GPT-4o-mini judge 0.515; finance prompt cut GPT-4o-mini 0.64 to 0.38
incremental_to: Prompt and rendering variants; single judge vs panel
informs_decision: Open analyst-question set on US filings with category split; judge-human agreement only 0.75 on three classes, so rubric items stay a minority with their own validation

citation: Koncel-Kedziorski, Krumdick, Lai, Reddy, Lovering & Tanner (2024), arXiv 2311.06602v2 (BizBench). Read: abstract page
text_source: Financial QA data, newly collected and augmented; eight tasks
feature: Quantitative reasoning by code generation; sub-tasks for extracting values and for knowing financial formulas; numeric (auto-gradable)
method: Open and commercial LLMs; code vs language models
outcome: Authors: bottleneck is business and financial understanding, not arithmetic
informs_decision: Separates value extraction from formula knowledge; same split as FinIndices' hint arm. FinCoT source

citation: Reddy, Koncel-Kedziorski, Lai, Krumdick, Lovering & Tanner (2024), arXiv 2401.06915v3 (DocFinQA). Read: abstract page
text_source: 7,437 FinQA questions paired with full filings; mean context about 123K words (FinQA under 700). CC BY-NC-SA 4.0
feature: Long-document numeric QA; auto-gradable
method: Retrieval pipelines and long-context models
outcome: Hard for state-of-the-art systems; worst on the longest documents
informs_decision: Long context adds difficulty without adding judgement; not the reasoning S1 needs

citation: Tang, E, Ma, He, Liu and 8 others (2025), ACL 2025 Long, pp. 15721-15749; arXiv 2506.05828v2 (FinanceReasoning). Read: abstract page and v2 HTML
text_source: 2,238 problems: updated CodeFinQA, CodeTAT-QA, FinCode, FinanceMath plus 908 new GPT-4o-generated expert-verified; Easy 1,000, Medium 1,000, Hard 238; 3,133 Python formula functions
feature: Numeric financial reasoning; strict auto-grading within 0.2%; CoT parsed by GPT-4o-mini, PoT executed
method: Reasoning and non-reasoning LLMs; CoT vs PoT; formula retrieval
outcome: o1 PoT 89.1% on Hard; GPT-4o 83.2 to 91.6 with formula functions; smallest model tested QwQ-32B (Hard CoT 63.5)
incremental_to: CoT vs PoT; with vs without formula library
informs_decision: Numeric reasoning near saturation for frontier models; formula library = knowledge hint; no small models

citation: Xie, Orel, Thareja, Sahnan and 21 others (2026), arXiv 2506.02515v4 (FinChain). Read: abstract page and v4 HTML (main tables)
text_source: 290 parameterised symbolic templates with executable Python, 58 topics, 12 domains; 2,900 test cases; Basic, Intermediate, Advanced
feature: Verifiable chain-of-thought: ChainEval = step alignment (DTW, numeric-gated) plus final answer within 5%; fully automatic
method: 26 models incl. finance-tuned and math-tuned 7-8B
outcome: GPT-5 ChainEval 66.57 / final 82.03; Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct 60.35 / 65.41; Fin-R1 58.14 / 52.76; Fin-o1-8B 41.50 / 52.79; tuned 7B models drop sharply on Advanced
incremental_to: Frontier vs domain- and math-tuned small models
informs_decision: Step-level auto-grading is possible for computations; finance tuning does not beat a plain 7B instruct model; gap opens with step count

citation: Mateega, Georgescu & Tang (2025), arXiv 2501.18062v1 (FinanceQA). Read: abstract page
text_source: Tasks modelled on hedge-fund, private-equity and banking work; Hugging Face
feature: Hand-built metrics, accounting and valuation conventions, multi-step tasks requiring self-generated assumptions; grading not read
method: LLM evaluation; GPT-4o fine-tuning via API
outcome: Models fail about 60% of tasks
informs_decision: Assumption-generation items are a distinct reasoning type; grading of assumption items needs checking before reuse

citation: Patel, Chen, He, Wang, Li, Xiao & Liu (2025), arXiv 2512.08270v1 (Reasoning Models Ace the CFA Exams). Read: abstract page
text_source: 980 mock CFA questions: three Level I, two Level II, three Level III exams
feature: MCQ and Level III constructed response; grading of constructed response not read
method: State-of-the-art reasoning models, prior pass criteria
outcome: Most models pass all levels; Gemini 3.0 Pro 92.0% on Level III constructed response
informs_decision: CFA-style items are near saturation for frontier models; may still separate 0.8B from 4B

citation: Mahfouz, Callanan, Sibue, Papadimitriou, Ma, Liu & Zhu (2024), EMNLP 2024 Industry, pp. 1068-1082. Read: ACL Anthology abstract page
text_source: Mock CFA exams, Levels I-III, MCQ and essays
feature: Financial analysis knowledge and essays; five proprietary and eight open models
method: Benchmarking; textbook data added for open models
outcome: Proprietary models pass I and II, fail III because of essays; open models below pass marks; textbook data narrows gap less at II and III
informs_decision: Essay (synthesis) items are where smaller open models fall furthest behind; domain text helps less at higher levels

citation: Yao, Wang, Liu & Huang (2025), arXiv 2509.04468v1 (CFA-based benchmark study). Read: abstract page
text_source: 1,560 MCQ from official CFA mock exams, Levels I-III
feature: MCQ (auto-gradable); zero-shot vs hierarchical RAG over CFA curriculum
method: Multimodal, reasoning and lightweight models
outcome: Reasoning models best zero-shot; RAG helps most on complex scenarios; knowledge gaps are the main failure mode
informs_decision: Knowledge, not readability, limits performance; supports a formula/definition-sheet arm

citation: Agrawal, Dutta, Hasan, Karmaker & Dutta (2026), arXiv 2603.19225v6 (FinTradeBench). Read: abstract page
text_source: 1,400 questions on NASDAQ-100 stocks over ten years, from 150 expert seeds; Core400 fully expert-reviewed
feature: Fundamentals, trading-signal and hybrid cross-signal questions; grading not read
method: Zero-shot plus retrieval, tool computation, oracle and time-series pipelines
outcome: Trading-signal questions harder than fundamentals; computation and evidence selection drive failures; retrieval helps signals not fundamentals
informs_decision: Integration of filings with price data is a separate reasoning type; mostly outside S1's EX-99.1 scope

citation: Dai, Lin, Xie & Wang (2026), arXiv 2602.07096v2 (RealFin). Read: abstract page
text_source: Bilingual exam-style finance questions with essential premises removed
feature: Answer / identify missing information / reject unjustified options; grading not read
method: Evaluation of general and finance-specialised models
outcome: Accuracy drops when premises are missing; general models over-commit, finance models rarely flag missing premises
informs_decision: Missing-premise items test judgement and can be graded by option choice; complements FinIndices traps

citation: Zhao, Long, Jiang, Wang, Chen, Liu, Zhang, Tang, Zhao & Cohan (2024), EMNLP 2024; arXiv 2411.05764v1 (FinDVer). Read: abstract page
text_source: 2,400 expert-annotated claims over long hybrid text-table financial documents
feature: Claim verification with explanation: information extraction, numerical reasoning, knowledge-intensive reasoning; verdict auto-gradable
method: Long-context and RAG settings; CoT analysis
outcome: GPT-4o best, below human experts
informs_decision: Entailment-style true/false claims about a document: an auto-gradable judgement format

citation: Guo & Yang (2024), Findings of ACL 2024; arXiv 2407.01212v1 (EconNLI). Read: abstract page
text_source: Premise-hypothesis pairs of economic events
feature: Causal economic inference (classification) and generation of consequences
method: LLM evaluation
outcome: LLMs show limited economic reasoning and hallucinate
informs_decision: Causal 'does A lead to B' items are auto-gradable as classification; the generation half is not

citation: Lu, Guo, Zhang, Zhu & Liu (2025), arXiv 2505.19457v1 (BizFinBench). Read: abstract page
text_source: 6,781 Chinese business-finance queries, nine categories
feature: Numerical calculation, reasoning, information extraction, prediction recognition, knowledge QA; objective metrics plus IteraJudge LLM judge
method: 25 models
outcome: No model leads everywhere; Qwen2.5-VL-3B far behind on calculation; Qwen3-1.7B lowest on extraction; open models trail by up to 19.5 on reasoning
informs_decision: Includes 1.7B-3B models: they trail most on calculation and extraction

citation: Wang, Qian, Peng, Ren, Wang and 16 others (2026), arXiv 2505.20650v5 (FinTagging). Read: abstract page
text_source: Financial reports, US GAAP XBRL taxonomy (over 10,000 concepts)
feature: Numeric identification (FinNI) and concept linking (FinCL) to the taxonomy
method: Zero-shot LLM evaluation
outcome: Good at extraction, weak at fine-grained concept linking
informs_decision: XBRL tasks are extraction and classification, not analysis; low priority for a reasoning exam

citation: Zhu, Chen, Dou, Li, Guo, Chen & Zhang (2025), arXiv 2504.15716v1 (DianJin-R1). Read: abstract page
text_source: CFLUE, FinQA and a proprietary Chinese compliance corpus (CCC)
feature: Reasoning-tuned financial models 7B and 32B
method: SFT with structured reasoning then GRPO (format and accuracy rewards)
outcome: Beat non-reasoning counterparts, esp. complex tasks; single call matches multi-agent systems on CCC
informs_decision: Another in-distribution gain; DianJin-R1-7B falls below its base on DocMath long tasks (qian-2025) and scores low on FinIndices (tong-2026, 32B)

citation: Hayrapetyan, Kalmykov, Kokosinskii, Stanishevskii & Zmitrovich (2026), arXiv 2609.10113v1. Read: abstract page
text_source: Mined reasoning traces, distilled finance instructions, knowledge-graph QA from educational material
feature: Retention-aware financial post-training; FINESSE-Bench
method: SFT vs self-distilled SFT vs merging vs GRPO on verifiable tasks
outcome: Plain SFT -3.2 to -4.0 points; self-distilled SFT +1.0 to +2.8; merging +0.9 net; GRPO +0.4 after SFT or +3.0 directly
informs_decision: Naive SFT can erase general ability; relevant if S1 distils on reasoning items

citation: Yue, Chen, Lu, Zhao, Wang, Song & Huang (2025), NeurIPS 2025; arXiv 2504.13837v5. Read: abstract page
text_source: Comparable domain: math, code, visual reasoning benchmarks
feature: Does RL with verifiable rewards add reasoning beyond the base model (pass@k at large k)
method: Several model families and six RLVR algorithms vs base and distilled models
outcome: RLVR wins at k=1, base wins at large k; RLVR gains bounded by base; distillation can add new reasoning patterns
informs_decision: An RL arm for the S1 student should be expected to sharpen, not add capability; distillation is the lever

citation: Khaybullina (2026), arXiv 2610.22043v1 (Momentum, Commentary Tone, and Earnings Surprise in LLM Financial Forecasts). Read: abstract page
text_source: Synthetic earnings announcements varying 20-day momentum, commentary tone and EPS vs a manipulated consensus; 2,016 prompts per model
feature: Which inputs move a small model's forecast; answer-prefix score shifts
method: Six instruct checkpoints 0.49B-7.61B, Q8_0 quantised, direct answers
outcome: In five of six models both tone and momentum contrasts exceed the EPS-surprise contrast; number recognition 51.0-95.8%
informs_decision: Small models' directional calls can rest on tone and momentum rather than the number; S1 direction items need tone-controlled pairs

citation: Shu (2025), M.S. final project, Northwestern University (Computer Science), not peer reviewed. Read: full text (PDF)
text_source: Compustat annual statements 1971-1979, 5,000 sampled firms; anonymised two-year BS and three-year IS (Kim et al. setup)
feature: Next-year EPS direction from statements, CoT prompt; direction label (auto-gradable)
method: Qwen2.5-1.5B, Qwen2.5-Coder-1.5B, R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, no fine-tuning; scaled-input robustness check
outcome: F1 63.03 / 68.44 / 64.27 vs GPT-4 73.28 and analysts 72.71 copied from Kim et al.; halving all numbers: 67.21
incremental_to: Baselines copied from withdrawn Kim et al.; no majority-class baseline
pit_handling: 1970s data and anonymisation inherited from Kim et al.; memorisation probe is input scaling only
informs_decision: Only small-model test of the Kim task found, and uninformative: F1 on imbalanced labels with no majority baseline; baseline paper withdrawn
